goal: Test whether high abundance of remaining host attenuates butterfly local extinction after decline of a different host, beyond host abundance and ordinary spatial differences.

source.citation: DiLeo et al. 2024 demography and environment modulate genetic-diversity extinction risk

botany.botanical_status: both established hosts in Åland, not an introduced-versus-native pair
botany.cover_unit: 0-3 observer ordinal per plant; not comparable edible biomass or per-capita larval quality

preexisting_evidence.claim: Opedal et al. (2020) already modeled 19 years of butterfly extinction and colonization with both host abundances plus connectivity; botanical quantity effects are prior art.
Hanski and Singer (2001) already linked colonization to host use and landscape host composition; matching preference is prior art.
Plant richness and butterfly diet specialization associations do not establish local functional fallback.

panel.select: one autumn record per Patch × Year; any unresolved duplicates fail source gate
panel.tminus1_definition: previous autumn t-1 with exact-year continuity
panel.tplus1_definition: next autumn t+1 with exact-year continuity
panel.risk_set: occupied(t)=1 and all three survey years observed; transition of hosts t-1 to t predates subsequent extinction at t+1
panel.source_limit: non-detection is not proven local extinction

events.comparison: within focal-host decline events, high versus low contemporary backup availability
events.negative_control: compare stable/nondeclining focal host cases using same backup strata

inference_if_pass.primary: difference in heldout network-block predictive logloss: base includes current Pl, Vs, Area, Nest_count and year; augmented adds decline×backup interaction; no tuning after effect inspection
inference_if_pass.secondary: observed extinction risk contrast with network bootstrap CI within decline stratum; compare stable host reference
confounds: drought and current edible plant stage
survivor selection from requiring occupied t
boundaries: not historical genetic or maternal hysteresis
many patch-years are not independent populations
host cover scores are ordinal, not true equal biomass
inference_if_pass.stop: If few independent real declines or no comparator overlap, close the observational fallback route rather than regressions and cut-off searches.

publication_decision: one existing one-species time series cannot establish a general causal butterfly ecological rule without independent replicated systems or experimental loss
